content: You are currently taking this medication. It is important to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments to monitor your progress and ensure the medication is working effectively. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store the capsules or tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store them in the bathroom. If you are using the liquid suspension form of this medication, keep it refrigerated and discard any unused portion after 14 days. Do not freeze the suspension. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of expired or unused medication. This medication is used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as cephalosporin antibiotics. It is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. Take this medication by mouth, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once or twice daily. If you are using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each dose. Measure the dose carefully using a special measuring device or spoon. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. Continue taking the medication for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Before taking cefadroxil, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to penicillins, or to other cephalosporins, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Cefadroxil may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. The liquid suspension may contain sugar, so caution is advised if you have diabetes or any condition requiring you to limit sugar intake. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. It passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may cause false positive results with certain diabetic urine testing products (e.g., cupric sulfate-type tests) and may also affect the results of certain laboratory tests. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Do not use it for another infection unless directed by your doctor. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as kidney function tests) may be performed while you are taking this medication to monitor your progress. Be sure to keep all medical and laboratory appointments.
